item: Democrats won the Texas governorship; Abbott had paused new rural AI data centres. Texas was due to host about a quarter of new US data-centre capacity by 2030.
note: Inference: power/permitting risk for grid-dependent leveraged builders; raises the value of on-site power (gas turbines, microreactors).

item: US midterms: Democrats won House (~255) and Senate (~55). Nasdaq-100 futures -2%, Nikkei ~-4% on the night.
A Democratic Senate makes extension of expiring OBBB tax cuts (from late 2028) less likely.

NVIDIA reportedly told data-centre partners (verbally) that at least 51% of revenue must come from non-China clients; also reports about Jensen Huang's ties to a person linked to Chinese intelligence.
Saudi Aramco Q3 profit +35% on high oil prices while Saudi GDP shrank 3.8%; plot against Syria's Homs refinery foiled.
US ammonia imports from Trinidad down 34%, adding to fertiliser inflation.
Trump says $4bn/yr military aid to Israel will wind down by year-end, earlier than the 2028 expiry.
Iran's energy-squeeze strategy: US gasoline above $4, diesel above $6. Democrats can cut Pentagon funding to pressure an end to the Iran war.
note: Bears on H2 kill signal K2 (Hormuz/Iran deal collapsing diesel prices).

item: Trump 2.0 pivoting to stabilise US-China ties: trade-truce renewals, flexibility on chip controls, 'transactional' noises on Taiwan.
Trump may push Ukraine toward land-for-peace; possible Xi/Putin meetings at APEC; US pushing Europe to fund US arms for Ukraine (PURL).
note: Inference: tilts defense spending toward Europe/NATO.

item: Indonesia: Prabowo deployed 20,000+ troops to Jakarta after arresting aides; 'market jitters'.
US claimed strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz; Vance says a deal 'could be close'; US fuel prices at records.
Hackers sabotaged supermarket refrigeration in six European countries; Russia suspected, possibly testing NATO Article 5.
Belgium near government collapse over an $11bn budget gap; debt >108% of GDP; borrowing costs at 15-year highs.
GMO Internet Group (9449.T) ransomware hit its cloud/forex platform; its 2031 bond spreads widened 50bp.
Direct Ukraine-Russia talks confirmed for Abu Dhabi next week; Trump may want a deal at APEC or G20.
ISW: Russia lost net territory in Ukraine for a second month; Ukraine claims a record 54,000 Russian casualties.
Xi's purges leave the Central Military Commission with two members; 71 senior officials under investigation in nine months; fourth term expected at the 2027 Party Congress.
Turkey detained 85 members of a network linked to Russian arson at a Starlink ground station in Poland.
Speculation Netanyahu (caretaker PM) could join US in resuming strikes on Iran; Cambodia cruise costs jumped after Hormuz squeeze.
Houthis claimed another hit on Saudi Ras Tanura refinery; crude +1.62%.
Woodside selling its 33% Greater Sunrise gas stake to Timor-Leste's state firm.

Indonesia: Prabowo deployed 20,000 troops to Jakarta after investigators say his chief of staff (ex-police chief Listyo) ran unauthorised surveillance on him. The rupiah is at record lows, the central bank governor quit early in July, and MSCI has threatened a downgrade over the opaque equity market.
note: Inference: rising EM/SE Asia risk premium; the Iran-war energy shock is hitting importers.

item: Trump after hosting Putin's envoy: a 'big agreement' coming that 'might involve all of Europe'; Russia-Ukraine talks resume in Abu Dhabi next week.
note: Inference: a ceasefire would change the defense-tech demand story (Anduril, GA, drones).

item: 21+ flights across Europe got fake bomb threats on Thursday, the third day of hoaxes this week.
Leaked documents show Russia plans to supply Iran with 90 helicopter-mounted LMUR missile launchers.
note: Inference: points to a longer Iran war, so oil and diesel stay high; works against H2's Hormuz/Iran-deal kill signal.

item: South Korea is expanding naval operations toward Hormuz and Somalia (anti-piracy, mine clearing). The Iran war has drained Western naval capacity and Somali piracy is filling the gap; Korea imports nearly all its oil.

France: 600k-1.5m on strike over wages and the cost of living, six months before elections Le Pen is forecast to win; Paris must choose between concessions that worsen its fiscal crisis and growing protests.
note: Inference: adds to European sovereign stress (with Belgium, Nov 3).

item: Paraguay: President Peña resigned after the collapse of digital bank Ueno (about 10% of the state pension fund's portfolio); he had resisted pressure to drop recognition of Taiwan.
note: Inference: small risk to one of Taiwan's few diplomatic allies.
